sources.claim: Self-employed people generally pay self-employment tax (Social Security and Medicare) on net earnings, and may need to make estimated tax payments during the year. The course teaches the idea only; rates and thresholds change and are not taught as current figures.
Tax is pay-as-you-go: people who do not have enough tax withheld, such as many self-employed people, may need to pay estimated tax in installments during the year.

sections.skill: Explain self-employment tax and why estimated payments exist

questions.prompt: What does withheld mean for an employee's paycheck?

choices.text: Her taxes are cancelled for the year
Her boss keeps her bonus as a reward
Her paycheck is held by the bank for a month
Taxes are taken out before she is paid

questions.correct_answer: Taxes are taken out before she is paid
questions.intro: An employee usually has taxes WITHHELD (taken out) from each paycheck. A self-employed person usually does not, so two ideas matter. SELF-EMPLOYMENT TAX covers Social Security and Medicare on net earnings from self-employment; an employer would normally pay part of these for an employee, but a self-employed person pays them. ESTIMATED TAX PAYMENTS: because tax is pay-as-you-go, a self-employed person may need to send payments during the year instead of waiting until the return. This course teaches the ideas; rates and deadlines change, so check the IRS.
questions.feedback: Withholding pays tax during the year.

questions.intro: Think of a bus pass you top up every month versus waiting to pay for a whole year of rides at once. An employee's taxes are topped up every paycheck by the employer.
